ra: Jupiter Dolichenus is one of the Near-Eastern cults in Roman dress grouped under the Eastern-cults hub.
Jupiter Heliopolitanus (Baalbek triad) belongs to the Roman Eastern-cults grouping.
Venus Heliopolitana, member of the Baalbek triad, belongs to the Roman Eastern-cults grouping.
Mercury Heliopolitanus, member of the Baalbek triad, belongs to the Roman Eastern-cults grouping.
Dea Syria is among the oriental cults of Roman religion in the Eastern-cults grouping.
Dea Caelestis is one of the Eastern (African/Punic) cults grouped under the Roman Eastern-cults hub.
Sol Invictus Elagabal, the Emesene solar cult in Roman dress, belongs to the Eastern-cults grouping.
Within the Heliopolitan triad of Baalbek, Venus Heliopolitana is the female consort of the chief god Jupiter Heliopolitanus.
Mercury Heliopolitanus is generally read as the youthful divine son of the Heliopolitan triad, with Jupiter Heliopolitanus as the father-figure.
Mercury Heliopolitanus is read as the divine son of the triad, completing the father-mother-son structure with Venus Heliopolitana as mother.
Jupiter Dolichenus is a Roman cult-epithet/form of Jupiter Optimus Maximus assimilating the Baal of Doliche.
Jupiter Heliopolitanus is the local Baalbek cult-form of Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
Venus Heliopolitana is the Heliopolitan local cult-form of Venus, assimilating the Syrian goddess of Baalbek.
Mercury Heliopolitanus is the Heliopolitan local cult-form of Mercury, assimilating the youthful Syrian son-god.
Dea Syria is the Roman cult reception of the Aramean goddess Atargatis of Hierapolis; Lucian's De Dea Syria names her so.
Dea/Juno Caelestis is the Romanized interpretatio identification of Carthaginian Tanit, the standard equation.
Dea Caelestis is the Roman reception/cult-form of the Punic goddess Tanit after the Romanization of Carthage.
Sol Invictus Elagabal is the Roman imperial cult reception of the Emesene sun-god Elagabal, whose baetyl emperor Elagabalus brought to Rome.
Elagabalus's short-lived Sol Invictus Elagabal (218-222 CE) is the solar precursor to and shares the Sol Invictus title with Aurelian's official Sol Invictus (274 CE), though they are distinct cults.
The underlying figure of Jupiter Dolichenus is the Commagenian storm-god of Doliche, a Baal-Hadad type; he is syncretized with the Canaanite/Syrian storm-god Baal Hadad.
Jupiter Heliopolitanus is the Romanized Baal/Hadad of Heliopolis (Baalbek), syncretizing the local Syrian storm-god with Jupiter.
The female member of the Baalbek triad underlies a local Syrian Atargatis/Astarte-type goddess, syncretized into Venus Heliopolitana.
